headline: Eggs, fish, and meat prices rise in Dhaka kitchen markets; some vegetables stable
summary: Broiler chicken, red eggs, hilsa, and other fish have seen price hikes, while most vegetable prices remain unchanged in the capital's markets. Sugar, flour, and polao rice also increased over the past month.
details: Prices of essential food items like eggs, fish, and meat have significantly increased in Dhaka's kitchen markets, including Shewrapara, Kazipara, Ibrahimpur, Farmgate, and Karwan Bazar. In contrast, prices for most vegetables have remained stable.

Over the past week, broiler chicken prices rose by Tk 10 per kg, now retailing at Tk 190-200. Beef is up to Tk 800-820 a kg from Tk 780-800, and a dozen red eggs now cost Tk 150-160, a Tk 10 increase. Mutton and goat meat prices, however, remain unchanged.

Despite being the peak season when prices typically fall, hilsa fish has seen a Tk 50 per kg increase, now selling for Tk 2,300-2,500 per kg. Prices of other fish varieties have also risen by Tk 10-20 a kg.

The vegetable market has shown relative stability for two weeks, with most items selling between Tk 40-120 per kg depending on quality. Papaya, okra, sweet pumpkin, teasel gourd, pointed gourd, taro root, bitter gourd, brinjal, ribbed gourd, sponge gourd, and bottle gourd prices are unchanged from last week.

However, yardlong beans have seen an increase, now priced at Tk 100-160 a kg. Beyond fresh produce, prices for sugar, flour, soap, coconut oil, and polao rice (now Tk 220-230 per kg) have also climbed over the last month.

Consumers express frustration over the rising costs, noting that even egg sizes have become smaller. Many find hilsa unaffordable despite it being the peak season, with concerns that a government pay scale implementation could further escalate essential prices.

A gas crisis is also impacting households, leading to reduced vegetable consumption and, consequently, lower sales for vendors. This decline in demand is cited as a reason why vegetable prices have not increased significantly.

headline_marked: [[70-year-old woman dies]] after being hit by state minister’s car in Bogura
headline: 70-year-old woman dies after being hit by state minister’s car in Bogura
summary: A 70-year-old woman died after being hit by a car carrying State Minister Abdul Bari in Bogura's Shibganj. The minister's SUV swerved, injuring him and his wife.
details: A 70-year-old woman, Firoza Begum, died after being hit by a car carrying State Minister for Public Administration and Food Abdul Bari and his wife in Bogura’s Shibganj upazila yesterday morning. The accident happened around 9:00am in Gopinathpur as the minister traveled from Dhaka to Joypurhat.

The state minister sustained an injury to his right leg when the SUV swerved off the Bogura-Joypurhat road and fell into a paddy field while trying to avoid hitting the woman. His wife also suffered minor injuries in the incident.

Firoza was initially taken to a local clinic before being transferred to TMSS Medical College and Rafatullah Community Hospital in Bogura. She died around 11:45am while undergoing treatment, having sustained a broken leg and injuries to her hand and head.

Firoza’s nephew stated that his aunt was crossing the road to visit her daughter’s house after a police protocol van had passed. The minister was later taken to Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital and is now on his way to Dhaka for advanced treatment.

No case has been filed regarding the accident and Firoza Begum’s death, but a General Diary has been recorded. The Shibganj Upazila administration has provided Tk 25,000 to the victim’s family for burial.
